skill.name: connecting-to-logseq
skill.description: Guides setup and troubleshooting for connecting AI assistants to Logseq through the HTTP API, CLI, or MCP server.
skill.summary: Connect AI assistants to Logseq with HTTP API, CLI, and MCP setup guidance.
skill.author: C0ntr0lledCha0s

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives from Markdown examples that target Logseq's localhost API or use inline code formatting. I confirmed one token exposure risk where instructions print LOGSEQ_API_TOKEN, and added semantic findings for unsafe write defaults. No prompt injection language was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Troubleshooting guidance can reveal the full Logseq API token.
remediation.suggestion: Replace token echo commands with masked presence checks, and never ask agents to print full token values.

remediation.issue: Example configuration disables write confirmations and backups.
remediation.suggestion: Set confirmWrites and backupBeforeWrite to true by default, and require explicit user approval for write methods.

remediation.issue: Setup guidance includes package installs, npx usage, build commands, and local script execution.
remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation before running commands, and document package verification steps for external dependencies.

remediation.issue: The main guide references setup scripts that are not present in the scanned package.
remediation.suggestion: Include the referenced scripts or remove the execution instructions to avoid unknown path execution.

semantic_findings.title: Logseq API Token Disclosure
semantic_findings.description: Troubleshooting guidance includes commands that can print LOGSEQ_API_TOKEN into terminal output or assistant transcripts. This can expose a reusable Logseq API credential.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The files explicitly tell users to echo the token value during authentication troubleshooting. That creates a clear credential exposure path in logs or chat transcripts.

semantic_findings.title: Write Safety Disabled by Default
semantic_findings.description: The skill documents Logseq write methods while the example configuration sets confirmWrites and backupBeforeWrite to false. Assistant-driven writes could modify graph data without confirmation or backup.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented methods include insertBlock and other graph operations, and the shown defaults disable confirmation and backups. The risk follows directly from the provided configuration.

content.value_statement: Connecting an AI assistant to Logseq requires tokens, backend choices, and graph path checks. This skill guides setup, API calls, CLI use, MCP configuration, and connection troubleshooting.
actual_capabilities: Guides users through enabling the Logseq HTTP API and creating authorization tokens.
Documents localhost API request formats for Python, JavaScript, and cURL examples.
Explains Logseq CLI installation, graph queries, exports, validation, and in-app mode.
Shows MCP server setup steps for exposing Logseq operations as assistant tools.
Troubleshoots connection refused, unauthorized, graph path, query syntax, and MCP failures.
Provides an example environment configuration for backend selection and token storage.
limitations: HTTP API and MCP workflows require Logseq to be running with developer mode enabled.
CLI workflows depend on a separate Logseq CLI installation and valid graph paths.
The scanned package does not include the referenced setup scripts.
Example configuration disables write confirmations and backups unless the user changes it.

use_cases.title: Set up a personal Logseq connection
use_cases.description: Guide an individual through token setup, backend selection, and first connection checks.

use_cases.title: Build a local Logseq API workflow
use_cases.description: Use the documented request formats to plan assistant-assisted reads and writes through localhost.

use_cases.title: Diagnose failed Logseq integrations
use_cases.description: Work through port, token, graph path, CLI, query, and MCP server issues.

prompt_templates.title: Start Logseq Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me connect Claude Code to my Logseq graph. Ask which backend I want, then guide token, localhost API, and graph path setup.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Connection Errors
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose why Codex cannot connect to Logseq. Check whether Logseq is running, the HTTP API is enabled, and the token is present without printing it.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Backend
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare HTTP API, CLI, and MCP options for my Logseq workflow. Recommend one backend based on whether I need reads, writes, or offline access.

prompt_templates.title: Plan MCP Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a safe MCP-based Logseq integration for Claude. Include setup checks, token handling, write confirmation, and rollback steps.

output_examples.input: I need to connect Claude to my Logseq graph for the first time.
output: Confirms Logseq developer mode and HTTP API settings.
Asks how the user wants to store the token safely.
Chooses a backend based on whether writes are needed.

output_examples.input: Logseq returns unauthorized when my assistant tries to connect.
output: Checks whether a token exists without displaying the token value.
Verifies the authorization format and localhost endpoint.
Suggests creating a new token if the old one was revoked.

output_examples.input: I want to use Logseq from an automated workflow.
output: Compares CLI, HTTP API, and MCP options.
Highlights when Logseq must be running.
Recommends confirmation and backup steps before writes.

best_practices: Store API tokens in environment variables or secret managers, not committed configuration files.
Confirm every write operation and back up the graph before assistant-driven changes.
Keep the Logseq HTTP API bound to localhost and do not expose the port to a network.
anti_patterns: Printing the full Logseq API token in terminal output or assistant transcripts.
Running global package installs or npx commands without verifying the source package.
Disabling write confirmations and backups for workflows that modify graph content.

faq.question: Does this skill require Logseq to be open?
faq.answer: The HTTP API and MCP paths require Logseq to be open. The CLI path can work against local graph files.

faq.question: Can it write to my Logseq graph?
faq.answer: Yes, the documented HTTP API methods include write operations. Require confirmation and backups before using them.

faq.question: Where should I store the API token?
faq.answer: Store the token in an environment variable or secret manager. Do not commit it to a configuration file.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What backend should I choose?
faq.answer: Use HTTP API for live reads and writes, CLI for offline tasks, and MCP for assistant tool integration.

faq.question: What should I check when connection fails?
faq.answer: Check that Logseq is running, developer mode is enabled, the API server is on, and the token is valid.
